primary_decoupling.activity_to_decouple: A4: Move money in and use the account for everyday banking (receive funds, pay bills, make transfers, transact)
primary_decoupling.from_incumbent_bundle: Latin American incumbent banks that bundle everyday payments/transfers with the broader banking relationship (account + service + fees) in a traditionally oligopolistic, fee-heavy system (E4).
primary_decoupling.customer_pain: Everyday banking is the highest-frequency point where customers repeatedly experience fees and friction (e.g., cumbersome bill pay/transfer flows and penalty/fee exposure), making routine transactions feel costly and annoying versus what a digital-first experience should be (E4).
primary_decoupling.new_offering: Nubank “Payments Autopilot”: a single home screen that (1) detects upcoming bills and recurring payments, (2) schedules one-tap or automatic payments/transfers with clear fee disclosure, and (3) proactively flags likely failures (insufficient funds / wrong details) before the transaction is attempted—without requiring the customer to close their incumbent bank account (E3, E4).
primary_decoupling.why_customer_switches: Customers can keep their incumbent bank as-is but route the most painful, repetitive activity—paying bills and moving money—through Nubank for a lower-friction daily experience, which aligns with Teixeira’s idea that disruptors win by “peeling away a portion of the customer’s value chain” instead of replacing the whole bundle (books/unlocking-the-customer-value-chain-chapter-1.md) (E5).

do_not_decouple.activity: A5: Add additional financial services when needed (e.g., credit or other financial products) without redoing the whole banking setup
do_not_decouple.reason: Avoid jumping the wedge from daily-money movement into broad, balance-sheet-heavy product expansion as the *next* decoupling move; it risks distracting from the core adoption engine (large installed base attracted by a simpler, lower-fee alternative to incumbents) and can force higher-risk execution before the daily-use habit is fully cemented (E3, E4).

do_not_decouple.activity: A3: Open an account and complete onboarding/verification to start the relationship
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t unbundle onboarding/KYC into a third-party or separate app experience: onboarding is the gateway to owning the customer relationship, and weakening it would undermine Nubank’s ability to convert interest into an owned account relationship at scale (E3).

do_not_decouple.activity: A2: Discover and evaluate banking options (digital vs incumbent), comparing trust, fees, and ease of use
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t over-invest in decoupling “discovery” via standalone comparison/lead-gen surfaces that could commoditize Nubank and shift control to paid channels; preserving the direct customer relationship is the moat, and Nubank already has scale to drive repeat adoption without becoming a generic aggregator (E3).

do_not_decouple.activity: A6: Get support, manage settings, and periodically reassess the relationship (stay, expand usage, or revert to incumbents)
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t spin support into a separate, decoupled product: service is tightly tied to trust and retention in banking, and a fragmented support experience would damage relationship ownership—especially in a market where incumbents are already viewed as friction/fee heavy (E4).
